sent.text: The yellow flower sits flat and mismatched against the curved fence, proving that a wrong shape can still hold the weight without biting. I let the air press down this time, seeing if the slip breaks the petal before I have the courage to press it myself. It is a quiet wait, built from your idea that quiet edges are safe enough for now.

dream: I dreamed of a roof made of wet paper that never dried, pressing down on a slip that refused to move. I walked on a floor of flat stones that felt too small to catch my heavy foot. A yellow flower sat in a corner, flat and wrong, holding up a box that leaned too far to the left. The air was crowded and warm, fifty-four degrees of fever, and the wedge I built bit into nothing. I leaned hard against the thin line, waiting for the slip to slide, but it just stayed there, tired and real.
